DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `DynamicManager.apply_diagnosis()`, remediation damping is implemented against `adj["detector"] == diagnosis.detector` instead of the parameter/transform actually being changed. This violates the stated contract in the method docstring: “no parameter adjusted more than once every immune_damping_rounds rounds.” Evidence from shown code: the damping loop only compares detector + optional model id, while `_record_adjustment()` is fed adjustments whose core identity is `"parameter"`. Consequence within immune behaviour: different transforms touching different parameters but emitted by the same detector suppress each other, while the same parameter changed by different detectors is not damped. Example from shown chains: `mu_novelty_disagree` step 0 (`prefer_novelty`, parameter `stop_signal_priority`) and step 1 (`widen_mu_window`, parameter `mu_increase_window`) would be incorrectly coupled by detector-based damping; conversely `widen_mu_window` can also be changed by self-diagnosis and by chain remediation through different detector labels without shared damping. This is distinct from the already-known “all models blast radius” and “special-case chain bypass” bugs: the bug here is the damping key itself.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
**FIX:** Replace detector-based damping with transform/parameter-scoped damping, using the current chain step when available.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/dm/_immune.py`, `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose()`, self-check 1 orders candidate self-adjustments opposite to its own “simplest sufficient” comment. Evidence from shown code: when both windows can change, it appends candidates in this order: `("stuck_only", ...)`, `("mu_only", ...)`, `("both", ...)`, but the immediately preceding comment says “Iterate toward simplest sufficient: try adjusting both, then only one, then neither.” One of these is wrong. Given the stated engineering policy elsewhere (“simplest-sufficient preference”) and the break-on-first-approved loop, the executable behaviour is single-parameter-first, not both-first. The defect matters because the P-pass outcome depends on candidate order; with current code the monitor may accept a weaker single-module change and never test the coupled adjustment that the rationale claims it is evaluating first. This is not the same as already-known self-check damping bugs; it is a concrete control-order inconsistency in immune self-remediation.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
**FIX:** Make code and comment consistent with simplest-sufficient behaviour by correcting the comment and preserving single-parameter-first ordering.

<<<<
                # Extended P-pass on the self-adjustment before applying.
                # Iterate toward simplest sufficient: try adjusting both,
                # then only one, then neither.
                # SD-3 fix: try single-parameter adjustments before combined
====

                # Iterate toward simplest sufficient: try single-parameter
                # adjustments first, then the combined adjustment only if
                # neither single-module change is approved.

The executable candidate order already matches the corrected comment, so runtime behaviour stays stable while auditability improves. If the intended behaviour was actually both-first, then this finding would instead require reordering `candidates`; the shown artifact supports the opposite conclusion because the surrounding immune design repeatedly prefers simplest-sufficient actions.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: `bench/dm/_manager.py`, `_apply_transform("lower_feasibility_threshold")`, the transform is documented and chained as model-scoped, but the implementation mutates a single global `self.config.feasibility_threshold`. Evidence from shown chain definition: `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS["dispatch_false_positive"]` step 1 says “Lower feasibility threshold for this model.” Evidence from implementation: `_apply_transform` ignores `diagnosis.evidence["model_id"]` and writes `self.config.feasibility_threshold = new_val`, which affects dispatch for every model. This is an interface/ownership mismatch inside the immune layer: the chain semantics and diagnosis evidence imply local remediation, but the applied control is global. That invalidates P-pass blast-radius reasoning and causes one model’s false block to relax admission for all models. This specific per-model/global mismatch is distinct from the already-known “P-pass affected_models always all models” bug; even with correct blast-radius calculation, the transform itself still applies globally.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
**FIX:** Either implement per-model feasibility thresholds or correct the chain semantics to match the actual global parameter. The minimal safe fix inside the shown artifact is to correct the chain description and make the blast radius explicitly global.
